H1_lower_tampa.interpretation: Thalassia frequency clearly declined while total seagrass point occupancy declined much less and was not clearly different from zero. Non-Thalassia-only occupancy increased directionally but its interval slightly crossed zero, so the full frozen buffering rule did not pass.

H2_exact_point.interpretation: The predeclared Lower-versus-Old+Middle comparison was non-estimable because Lower had fewer than the frozen 20 loss events and 5 nodes. Descriptively, most exact-point Thalassia losses remained occupied by another seagrass in both groups.

ecological_boundary: The data suggest partial buffering of total seagrass occupancy during Lower Tampa Thalassia decline, but do not support a Lower-specific replacement advantage. Exact-point losses frequently retain another seagrass, motivating a separately frozen test of whether this reflects persistence of pre-existing mixed-species patches rather than new colonization.
claim_boundary: The full H1 support rule did not pass because non-Thalassia-only occupancy CI crossed zero.
H2 was non-estimable under its frozen event/node minima and must not be rescued by lowering them.
Target alternative species after Thalassia loss do not establish colonization; the species may already have co-occurred at the source point.
Do not interpret target alternative occupancy as competitive replacement or equivalent ecosystem function.
